subject: Post-call recap: ShopWise POC — add cart intent + revised success metrics
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@shopwise.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: ShopWise POC — next steps

Jordan — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery and suggested next steps so we’re aligned before the POC kickoff: 

Summary of the call
- Primary objective: validate a production-ready cart-intent signal in your storefront search/chat flows to prioritize conversion prompts and personalized offers.
- Current constraints: limited labeled cart-intent data (approx. 3k examples), strict latency target (<= 80ms p95), and black-box analytics requirement for auditability.
- Stakeholders: Jordan (Product), Ops team, and Emily (engineering, not on today’s call).

Suggested POC scope (initial)
1) Ingest sample events and label set (we’ll use the Eval_Set attached).
2) Deploy a two-week online A/B test using Redwood hosted endpoint + prefix KV cache.
3) Measure: recall@top1 for cart-intent, p95 latency, and % of sessions with correct action suggestion.

Immediate asks / next steps
- Jordan: share a CSV export of ~2k recent events (anonymized) and any existing labels.
- Rachel (me): send POC plan + rough timeline and success metrics (attached draft).
- Ben: scope cost/slot estimate and any Dedicated recommendations if we need throughput beyond hosted.

I attached a draft POC plan (ShopWise_POC_DRAFT.pdf) and an evaluation worksheet (ShopWise_Eval_Set.xlsx). If this looks right, I’ll turn this into a mutual action plan and propose dates for the kickoff.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with proposed kickoff slots next week.

—
Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: ShopWise_POC_DRAFT.pdf (plan), ShopWise_Eval_Set.xlsx (sample labels)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call recap: ShopWise POC — next steps

Rachel — saw your recap, looks solid. A couple quick internal notes: 
- Cost: for the 2-week online A/B with expected peak QPS of ~12, we can probably stay hosted but should include a Dedicated option in the MOP if they want contiguous low p95 across larger traffic spikes. I’ll sketch a 2-tier cost estimate (hosted vs dedicated) and drop it in the MAP doc.
- Compliance: ShopWise asked about auditability — recommend we include a short appendix on logging + retention (SOC2 signal). Marissa, can you confirm whether our standard logging retention language (30/90/365 days options) is okay to propose?

I’ll be available to join the kickoff to scope infra requirements.

—Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Note: internal-only comment, no external recipients on this message.

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@shopwise.io>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@shopwise.io
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 17:36:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call recap: ShopWise POC — next steps

Rachel — appreciate the recap. Two asks from our side after debriefing with ops/eng: 
1) Add a second use case to the trial: cart-intent signal + checkout-failure classifier. We think a combined signal will help route recovery offers.
2) Tighten success criteria: instead of recall@top1 alone, can we include lift-in-conversion (percentage lift for sessions routed to offer) and a false-positive ceiling (FP rate <= 6%)?

Constraints:
- We can only provide ~1.5k labeled cart-intent examples up front; engineering can add synthetic labels later.
- Timeline: their Q2 promo starts 2027-05-02, so we need results and a runbook by 2027-04-28 to make decisions. That shortens the window — can Redwood commit to a condensed timeline?

If we can accommodate the checkout-failure classifier and adjust success metrics, we’re keen to proceed. Please advise on feasibility and any tradeoffs (latency/accuracy/cost).

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Lee | Head of Product, ShopWise
jordan.lee@shopwise.io

Attachments referenced: none

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@shopwise.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, ops@shopwise.io
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call recap: ShopWise POC — add cart intent + checkout-failure classifier (rebaseline)

Jordan — great visibility and thanks for the timeline constraint. We can do a condensed rebaseline with the changes you requested. Proposed plan below (high level) — I’ll convert into a mutual action plan and update the attached deck & eval sheet.

Rebaseline summary (scope + ownership)
- New use cases: 1) Cart-intent detection (original), 2) Checkout-failure classifier (added).
- Success metrics: recall@top1 (cart-intent), conversion lift (A/B delta — primary business metric), FP rate <= 6% (both models), and p95 latency <= 95ms (note: adding classifier may increase compute slightly).
- Data: proceed with the 1.5k labeled examples now; ShopWise engineering to seed additional synthetic labels by 2027-04-10. We will run a rapid labeling audit and recommend upsampling strategies by 2027-04-07.

Timeline (condensed)
- 2027-04-05: Finalize MOP and sign-off on test traffic samples (both teams).
- 2027-04-06 to 2027-04-16: Rapid model iteration + offline eval.
- 2027-04-17 to 2027-04-24: Short online A/B (rolling test), collect conversion lift signals.
- 2027-04-25 to 2027-04-28: Final analysis + runbook for promo decision.

Owners and touchpoints
- Redwood: Rachel (SE lead, contact), Ben (commercial lead), infra support (optional Dedicated consult).
- ShopWise: Jordan (product), Ops/Eng (data & traffic).

Attachments and artifacts
- I will attach an updated evaluation worksheet and an updated plan (ShopWise_POC_DRAFT.pdf v2) once Ben confirms the cost appendix and Marissa confirms retention language.

Risks / tradeoffs
- Adding the checkout-failure classifier pushes the p95 target from 80ms to ~95ms at p95 on hosted; we can mitigate with KV caching and batching but will monitor impact.
- The condensed timeline means less time for drift testing — we’ll call out monitoring requirements in the runbook.

Next steps (this week)
- Jordan: confirm you can share the 1.5k export by Mon 2027-04-05.
- Ben: send the cost appendix and Dedicated recommendation by EOD Mon.
- Marissa: confirm logging/retention language and whether 90-day default is acceptable.
- Rachel: update the MOP and schedule kickoff for 2027-04-05 or 04-06 depending on availability.

If that all aligns I’ll push the updated artifacts to the Drive link and create the HubSpot mutual action plan entry: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/4521

—
